newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Privatisation of Bangladeshi jute mills faces snag.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation of Bangladeshi jute mills faces snag.

text.p: Bangladesh's State Minister for Jute and Textile A K Faezul Huq said on Saturday privatisation of state-owned jute mills slowed due to lack of buyers.
"Selling tenders for several mills receive poor response from buyers in many occasions. There was even not a single (valid) bid in case of some mills tendered," Huq told parliament.
He said the government had been making efforts to divest 10 state-owned jute mills since April 1994, but only two could be sold.
Bangladesh is restructuring its ailing jute industry under a $250 million World Bank credit programme.

Under its restructuring plan, Bangladesh aims to reduce loom capacity in some mills and close down heavy loss-makers. Bangladesh's nearly 35 state-owned jute mills incur $115 million in annual losses due to excess manpower, poor management, outdated machinery and falling international jute prices.
